name: The Thompson house
status: Canon 2 (address); design interpreted from reference/board-10.jpg crossed with board-02.jpg
style: Red-brick Colonial Revival, two stories plus dormers, with a garage wing
materials: red-brown running-bond brick with light mortar, projecting base course with a cast-stone cap
slate-grey slate-style roofing, copper flashing and downspouts
white painted trim: frieze with dentils, portico, cornice returns, dormers
cast-stone jack-arch lintels with keystones and stone sills
dark green six-panel entry door with brass hardware
notes: Main block 14.8 x 9.4 m, side-gabled at 40 deg, roof surface 7.0 m at the walls, ridge 10.9 m (Atlas height 8.5 m; within the 30% allowance). From board-10: the projecting front-gable bay on the left with a Palladian (arched centre) window and a half-round attic vent, the white pedimented entry portico, black shutters, slate-grey roof, interior end chimneys. From board-02: gabled dormers, jack-arch heads, copper accents. Interpreted: the 1.5-story front-gabled garage wing with carriage doors joined by a one-story hyphen on the right (the brief asks for a side garage wing), the rear one-story family-room wing and brick-and-stone terrace, side and rear elevations, the asphalt drive with a Belgian-block edge, the brick front walk to the curb, foundation beds, one big shade tree front left and a dogwood by the garage. No fence or hedge along the frontage (the lot owns its frontage; the walk and drive run to the curb line).
